Axolotl 0.2.0 adds type parameters, annotations, class literals, the type argument `*` and interface methods, so JUnit tests, Jackson
records and Spring entry points can be written in Axolotl, and comes with installers, which bring
their own Java runtime, and with `axl setup`, so the Gradle and Maven plugins no longer have to be
built from source.

## Downloads

The installers bring their own Java runtime, put `axl` on the `PATH` and run `axl setup`, which
copies the Axolotl libraries and the Gradle and Maven plugins into the local Maven repository:

- `axolotl-0.2.0-windows-x64-setup.exe`: Windows. Not signed, so SmartScreen asks first: *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
- `axolotl-0.2.0-macos-arm64.pkg`: macOS on Apple silicon. Not signed: see the [installation guide](https://github.com/succubus-uwu/axolotl/blob/v0.2.0/docs/install.md) for how to open it.
- `axolotl-0.2.0-linux-amd64.deb`: Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 or newer: `sudo apt install ./axolotl-0.2.0-linux-amd64.deb`.
- `axolotl-0.2.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`: other Linux systems. Unpack it and run `install.sh`, which needs no root.

Guides to installing and using the `axl` command line, in English and Russian:
`axolotl-0.2.0-windows-en.pdf`, `axolotl-0.2.0-macos-en.pdf`, `axolotl-0.2.0-linux-en.pdf` and the
`-ru` versions.

Without an installer:

- `axl-0.2.0.zip`: the command line compiler for Java 21. Unzip it, put `bin` on your `PATH` and run
  `axl setup` for the Gradle and Maven plugins.
- `axolotl-0.2.0.vsix`: the VS Code extension: `code --install-extension axolotl-0.2.0.vsix`.
- `axl-intellij-0.2.0.zip`: the IntelliJ IDEA plugin: *Settings | Plugins | Install Plugin from Disk*.

The Gradle and Maven plugins are not published to a public repository yet: `axl setup` installs them
into the local Maven repository, and projects find them there with `mavenLocal()`.

## What is new

- Annotations: `@Test fn parses()` in a `class`, `@JsonProperty("x") val x: Int` in a data class, and
  any other `@Name(args)` before a declaration go into the generated Java as they are. Class
  literals `String.class` and the type argument `*` (`Class<*>`) complete the Java interoperability,
  and `attempt X else e -> throw Y` calls a Java method with a checked exception where no `Result` is
  wanted.
- Interfaces require methods as well as values: `fn add(text: String) -> Int` without a body, which
  each class that implements the interface writes, with the nullness of the types checked.
- Type parameters: `data class Pair<A, B>(...)`, `interface Repository<K, V>`, `class Stack<T : Object>`
  and `fn largest<T : Comparable<T>>(xs: List<T>) -> T?`, so generic code no longer stays in Java.
- Custom exceptions and other Java subclasses: `class NotFound(val id: String) : RuntimeException(...)`;
  enum constants with fields; `break` and `continue`; `print` and `readLine`.
- `attempt conn.commit() else e -> throw IllegalStateException(e)` on a line of its own calls a
  method that returns nothing and declares a checked exception, `x ?: throw Y` throws when `x` is
  null, and a `Result` has `isOk()`, `map` and `getOrElse`. `is Ok` and `is Err` narrow a `Result`
  whose type the translator cannot see.
- `axl run -cp lib.jar Main.axl` runs a program that uses a library without a build tool.
- Editors know annotations, interface methods and `@Test` classes (run from the gutter in IntelliJ).
- Strict null mode trusts the JDK methods that never return null, and many error messages were
  reworded after an eighth review with four realistic programs.
- The installers and `axl setup`. The bundled runtime has every module of Java SE, so code that uses
  `java.awt` or `java.beans` compiles and runs.
- `--help` on every command, and `axl help`.
- `axlLspConfig` and `axl:lsp-config` write a module for each source set, and a Gradle module sees
  the sources of the projects it depends on. The format of `axl.json` changed with it; run the task
  again after upgrading.
- Fixes for Windows paths, non-UTF-8 locales and the build.
- Compiler fixes from seven rounds of review: a `when` over an `Int?` no longer unboxes null, `==`
  compares numbers from `?:` and `try` by value, initialization order and same-file `private` are
  checked, raw generic values from Java are rejected, and long `?:` chains and nested `if` values
  compile in linear time.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/succubus-uwu/axolotl/blob/v0.2.0/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

## Known limitations

- `var x = when` with lambdas in its branches needs a written type.
- Error Prone in Maven needs `.mvn/jvm.config`, and Gradle compiles in a forked JVM.
